localChanges: Settlers, Transports and other units with no attack strength can no longer attack, a fight they could only lose (closes #642).

log: feat: announce who ended a treaty

Every treaty this package ends names who ended it (declareWar's player, the player cancelling a treaty in a meeting, a computer player dropping a sham peace), and declaration/expired/announce passes that player on with diplomacy:declaration-expired and player:declaration-expired. Needs core-diplomacy's Declaration#expire(by). For civ-clone/web-renderer#641.
chore: require core-diplomacy 0.1.7
feat: a treaty partner's land, and the Senate

A move from land onto an improved tile (irrigation, mine, road or railroad) that a treaty partner's city works, by a land unit that isn't a Diplomat or a Caravan, and with none of the unit's own units there, is no longer a Move (civ-clone/web-renderer#287). It's offered as SneakMove (Break treaty) and AbortMove (Cancel: stay, and spend the move's cost, as v474.05 takes it before asking, CheckPlayerTurn.cs ~L1662-1705). Pillaging such a tile is a SneakPillage. Neither sets a Vendetta: v474.05 only clears Peace.

Under the Republic or Democracy every action that would break a treaty (sneak move, pillage, attack, nuclear attack, capture, steal technology, incite revolt) is offered as Overruled instead (civ-clone/web-renderer#133). An overruled move still spends its cost; anything else keeps the unit's moves.
The impassable/treaty-partners-land rule keeps routes off such tiles, so GoTo and computer players never break a treaty by accident.
getRules takes the PlayerGovernmentRegistry as a new last argument.
perf: check a treaty partner's land after the cheap criteria

Pillage's partner check comes after hasMovesLeft and isCurrentTile, and a move's looks up the worked tile before scanning the units on it. Tests that a route passing over a partner's land is blocked, and one ending there halts, without breaking the treaty.
feat: a treaty broken by a unit names its player

moved/break-peace-treaty expires the peace with the unit's player as the one who ended it (core-diplomacy's Declaration#expire(by)), so the announcement can tell the player who broke it from the one it was broken against (civ-clone/web-renderer#641).
fix: a unit with no attack can't attack

attackCriteria gains attack() > 0, after the check for a foreign unit since working out the attack runs the yield rules. Settlers and the Transport (attack 0) are no longer offered Attack or SneakAttack, nor an Overruled one under a Senate. v474.05 lets them attack and they always lose; Dom chose to drop that (civ-clone/web-renderer#642). Tests for this and for the treaty's breaker are in treaty.test.ts.
chore: require core-diplomacy 0.1.7, core-world-path 0.1.3, library-unit 0.1.14

Declaration#expire takes the player who ended it, if one did, and passes it to the Expired rules (now Rule<[Declaration, Player | null]>). It isn't kept, so saves don't change. For civ-clone/web-renderer#641: breaking a treaty yourself was announced as the other player's sneak attack.
A path finder leaves out any tile an Impassable rule says true for, unless the route ends there. civ1-unit uses it for a treaty partner's land (civ-clone/web-renderer#287).
For a treaty partner's land (civ-clone/web-renderer#287) and the Senate (civ-clone/web-renderer#133):

SneakMove: a move that breaks a treaty with enemy(). Not a Move, so nothing that takes any Move it's offered (GoTo, a computer player's step) breaks a treaty by accident. It costs what a Move onto the same tile would.
SneakPillage: a Pillage that breaks a treaty with enemy().
AbortMove: a move onto partner()'s land called off. The unit stays and spends the move's cost.

Overruled: offered in place of action(), which would break a treaty, when the player isn't free to. action() is never performed; it says what was asked for (its enemy, a Diplomat's price). Choosing it spends moves().
feat: computer players keep off a treaty partner's land

breaksTreaty is now any action with an enemy(), the same test civ1-unit's moved/break-peace-treaty rule ends the peace by, so SneakMove, SneakPillage, SneakInciteRevolt and SneakNuclearAttack are covered without a list. actionsToTake leaves out AbortMove and Overruled, which only spend moves, and a tile offering SneakMove, AbortMove or Overruled scores -10, as a sneak attack does (civ-clone/web-renderer#287, civ-clone/web-renderer#133).
chore: require library-unit 0.1.14
feat: routes go round tiles an Impassable rule blocks
canMoveTo asks the Impassable rules for every tile but the destination, the same exemption a tile held by another player gets (civ-clone/web-renderer#287).
